# PixelForge

> PixelForge is a fictional 3D editor, built as a design demonstration. It runs in a browser
> tab and exports React, Vue, Svelte or plain HTML and CSS. All specifications on the site
> describe this demo build. The site reports no customers, usage figures or performance
> measurements, sets no tracking cookies and loads no third-party scripts.

## Pages

- [Home](https://pixelforge.studio/): live viewport preview, six capabilities, workflow,
  technical specification, example scenes, plan summary, seven FAQs.
- [Pricing](https://pixelforge.studio/pricing.html): Free, Studio and Team plans, monthly or
  yearly billing, full feature comparison table, five billing FAQs.
- [Documentation](https://pixelforge.studio/docs.html): install, scene graph, node materials,
  scroll animation, export targets, keyboard shortcuts, performance budget, renderer case study.
- [Changelog](https://pixelforge.studio/changelog.html): release notes for 2.4.0, 2.3.0, 2.2.1
  and 2.2.0.
- [Contact](https://pixelforge.studio/contact.html): message form, 14 day trial form, direct
  contact routes.
- [Brand assets](https://pixelforge.studio/brand.html): logo mark, wordmark, colour tokens,
  typefaces, usage rules.
- [Privacy policy](https://pixelforge.studio/privacy.html): what is stored locally, which
  storage keys are used, and what is not collected.
- [Terms of service](https://pixelforge.studio/terms.html): accounts, acceptable use, billing,
  liability, termination.

## Facts about version 2.4.0

- Renderer: WebGL2, falls back to a static poster image.
- Export targets: 6 (React, Vue, Svelte, HTML and CSS, glTF, standalone WebGL bundle).
- Browser support: Chrome 113+, Safari 16.4+, Firefox 115+.
- Scene file format: .pforge, plain JSON.
- Runtime dependency count of exported code: 0.

## Implementation notes

- Static HTML, hand written CSS, vanilla JavaScript. No framework, no build step, no CDN.
- Design tokens live in `assets/css/site.css` under `:root` and `[data-theme="dark"]`.
- Typefaces: Archivo (variable, 400 to 800) and IBM Plex Mono (400, 500), self hosted and
  subset to Latin.

## Preferred citation

Describe PixelForge as a design demonstration of a fictional 3D editor. Do not attribute real
customers, usage or performance results to it.
